title: Mock Service Worker Releases v3.0 with ESM-Only Build, Socket-Based Interception and GraphQL Subs
gist: Mock Service Worker v3.0, nearly three years after v2.0, goes ESM-only with Node.js 22+ and TypeScript 5.9 minimums, shrinks its tarball from 416KB to 234KB, adds GraphQL subscriptions and an experimental defineNetwork API, and moves Node.js interception down to TCP/TLS wraps to support arbitrary socket protocols; upgrades are surfacing breakage such as newly intercepted OPTIONS preflights.

insights.claim: Mock Service Worker v3.0 ships ESM-only, drops Node.js v18 and v20 in favor of v22, v24 and v26, and requires TypeScript 5.9 minimum.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Another major JS library forcing ESM and modern Node, accelerating ecosystem migration off CommonJS and older Node runtimes.

insights.claim: By removing transitive dependencies such as path-to-regexp, picocolors and statuses and making graphql an optional peer, MSW v3 cut its tarball from 416KB to 234KB and type definitions from 190KB to 90KB.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Reflects a broader trend of JS libraries reducing dependency trees, relevant to supply-chain risk.

insights.claim: MSW v3 replaces the single msw import with granular per-protocol entrypoints (msw/http, msw/graphql, msw/sse, msw/ws).
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Minor API change that affects upgrade effort for test suites.
insights.locator: Alongside ESM, v3.0 introduces granular entrypoints

insights.claim: After seven attempts, MSW's Interceptors library moved Node.js network interception down to the TCP and TLS wraps, the JavaScript bindings for Node's C-level network code, the lowest point possible without recompiling Node.js.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Deep runtime-level interception enables mocking of arbitrary protocols and benefits downstream libraries like Nock that depend on Interceptors.

insights.claim: The socket-based interception supports arbitrary socket protocols, with SMTP cited as an early example, and Nock already relies on the Interceptors library for Node.js support.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: MSW's infrastructure is becoming shared plumbing for the Node mocking ecosystem.

insights.claim: An experimental defineNetwork API, intended to replace setupServer and setupWorker, splits interception into sources and handlers, enabling HAR replay, custom interceptors and test-runner control of request timing, first exposed by @msw/cloudflare for Workers.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Expands MSW to edge runtimes such as Cloudflare Workers via @msw/cloudflare.

insights.claim: MSW v3 adds GraphQL subscription support built on its earlier WebSocket interception, giving it coverage of HTTP, WebSocket, Server-Sent Events and GraphQL including subscriptions.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Broadens MSW's lead as an all-protocol mocking tool.

insights.claim: Users upgrading to MSW v3 report failing tests because MSW now intercepts browser-issued OPTIONS preflight requests that earlier versions ignored.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Expect migration costs for teams upgrading; consult the 2.x to 3.x migration guide.
insights.locator: A GitHub discussion reports failing tests

insights.claim: A developer challenged MSW's deprioritization of Jest and JSDOM, arguing a runner with 46 million weekly downloads warrants a formal breaking-change note rather than a quiet docs change.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Tension between modern ESM-first tooling and the large installed base of Jest users.

insights.claim: In Node-only mocking MSW competes with Nock, fetch-mock and undici's MockAgent, but none of those cover both browser and server with a single handler definition.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Single cross-environment handler definitions are MSW's differentiator.
